linkedin.about:
My overarching mission is to empower people to make choices in life from a point of awareness, not ignorance.

Over the past 18 years in the internet and technology space, I’ve had the privilege of working on several ventures - founding some, investing in others, and learning from all. 

Over 16 million people follow my work across social platforms, where I share my experiences and insights on career, mindset, startups, personal finance, and relationships.

Today, my main focus is building my 3 startups

1/ WebVeda.com
A growth platform, offering skills, community and jobs at an annual subscription. 
WebVeda has over 500,000 members as of May 2026

2/ India Genius Challenge
Nation-wide search for the brightest kids in India, through a 2-phase program. 
Winners of the IGC get a Rs. 10L scholarship towards their higher education. 

3/ Monzy.co
The place to find YOUR best credit card.
No ads. No sponsorships. No personal data sought or tracked. 

I’ve also written six bestselling books that have sold 1Mn+ copies worldwide across 63 countries and translated into 17 languages:
- Do Epic Shit (2022)
- Get Epic Shit Done (2023)
- Make Epic Money (2024)
- Build An Epic Career (2025)
- Beyond The Syllabus (2025): for teenagers only
- Winning People Without Losing Yourself (2026)

It’s been a journey shaped more by reflection and exploration than certainty, and I wouldn’t have it any other way.

positions.description:
There is a “best credit card” for all of us. 
The one that fits our needs perfectly. 
Monzy finds it for you. 

No ads. No sponsorships. No personal data sought or tracked.

India Genius Challenge (IGC) is a nationwide search for the brightest young mind in India. 

IGC comprises of 5-min daily online challenges (completely free of cost) where school kids earn Genius Points (GPs) and compete with kids across the country. 
Daily, Weekly, Monthly National winners get books, smartwatches, earphones, iPads, laptops. 

The top performers in the online challenges will be invited to the National Finals in Delhi, where the winner of IGC will win Rs. 10L of scholarship.

WebVeda is a growth platform offering skills, community and jobs for an annual subscription. 

It is my personal aim to make the highest quality education, the best community and the finest job opportunities available to everyone in India - irrespective of their pincode or background. 
Which is why a WebVeda subscription is affordable, comes with 100% refund policy and lifetime upgrades. 

As of May 2026, WebVeda has 500,000+ members

I create content on Personal Finance, Career, Relationships and Personal Growth. 
As of May 2026, I have 16.8M+ cumulative followers across platforms. 

I have been creating content since 2005 (my blog, which is still maintained). 
My LinkedIn journey started in 2013.
YT and IG in 2017.

All of this is possible because of my team @waricrew - a bunch of young, eager and curious minds.

I invest in growth stage startups, with a focus on consumer internet startups. 

I look for fearless teams with a strong risk appetite, willingness to get uncomfortable and curiosity that of a child! 
Connect with me on warikoo@gmail.com

posts.caption: Everybody is jealous of the destination. Nobody is jealous of the journey.

5 money rules my wife and I follow as a couple aged 45 with two kids.

1. We don’t spend money to look rich. 

We spend to become wealthy and gain freedom of our time.

So, there’s no car. It’s rented. 
We own the house we live in, no other real estate.

No spending on brands. No spending just to show off to people.

2. We spend extravagantly on high-quality food.

We know that what goes into our body is ultimately the biggest wealth we have, and unfortunately, healthy food is not cheap.

3. We spend on experiences more than things.

Things give you happiness once, and they have no end.

You remember experiences, and they make you a better person. 
You grow as a person.

We travelled 116 days last year!

4. We invest before spending.

As soon as our salary comes, the largest amount is invested.

The remaining amount is used for expenses.

We are recording this on the 30th. 
₹9,000 and ₹600 left in our bank accounts. 
Everything else is invested.

5. No budget for books and learning.

No amount of money spent is enough.

Ruchi is learning pottery, watercolor painting, and tennis.

Our kids also go to many classes.

These are our rules. 
They may not apply to you, but having your own rules is important in life.

Before you say yes to marriage, check these 5 things.

1. Why are you getting married? Is it for the sake of society? Is it for the sake of your parents? Is it for your own good?

2. How do you handle fights with your partner? Because fights will continue. If you handle them properly, then relationships will progress.

3. Do you have an alignment on money and responsibility? How will you spend money? How will you share responsibilities?

4. Do you have space for your own personality? You can make friends without involving their friends. You can live your own life without depending on them.

5. How will you spend your life after marriage? What are the expectations from your family? How will your daily routines be? What will be your living arrangements? What have you thought about your children?

This is an important decision. Don't take it in a hurry.

4 signs that your life is much better than you think.

1/ Someone in your family has stopped worrying about you - because they trust you now.

2/ Your 18-year-old self wouldn't believe where you've reached.

3/ People now ask you for advice about something you once used to panic about.

4/ One bad day doesn't ruin your entire week, one bad week doesn't ruin your month, and one bad month doesn't ruin your year.

Sometimes, you've already made more progress than you realise.

There's a difference we often miss.

Being dependent means you need them to function. 
Being dependable means they can count on you, and you on them, without either of you losing yourselves.

One comes from fear. 
The other comes from strength.

The strongest relationships aren't two people who can't live without each other.

They're two whole people who choose, every day, to be someone the other can rely on.

3 reasons we bought our first home at 40 and not at 25 or 30.

1/ By the time we hit 40, we knew we wanted to live in Delhi.

At 25 or 30, there’s so much flexibility in life to change cities, even change countries if you want to.

But by the time we reached 40, we already knew we’re going to stay here. That’s why we chose this place.

2/ At that time, we had enough money that we could afford its EMI and its down payment for the house we wanted to live in.

At 25 or 30, that house wasn’t affordable for us.

3/ The house we wanted to live in is a very premium apartment.

The locality we wanted to live in, the area we wanted - we knew all of that by the age of 40.

Because we’d already had kids, life had settled.

In your 20s and 30s, life is still moving, so you don’t know how big a house you need, which locality you’ll prefer, etc.

That’s why I often say - instead of buying a house at 25 or 30, delay it a little and buy a house at the right time.

Raunak spent years struggling to get his words out.

Today, he helps others find their voice. 

A story of resilience, transformation and finding strength in his own voice 💪

Should you tell your parents how much you earn?

There’s a case for yes. They raised you, supported you, and may have every reason to know.

But there’s another side.

Once they know your salary, expectations can change - a bigger house, a car, a trip, a higher contribution at home.

So instead of telling them exactly how much you earn, you could tell them what your money can do for them.

“I can contribute ₹X towards the house.”

“I can afford this trip.”

“I can cover this EMI.”

Tell them what your money can do, not necessarily how much you make.

A counterpoint of view - do you agree?

Some people don't add to your life. 
They slowly drain it.

The ones who confuse you. 
The ones who hurt you and call it a joke. 
The ones who take your energy and give nothing back.

We keep them around out of guilt, or history, or habit.

But protecting your peace isn't cold. 
It's necessary.

You're allowed to walk away from anyone who only knows how to take.

5 questions people ask - and how we hear them.

1/ “When are you getting married?”

We hear that nothing I’ve done in life so far means nothing until I get married.

2/ “How much do you earn now?”

We hear that my entire worth is based on one salary, one number, and that will give me a rank.

3/ “Sharma ji’s son, well…”

We hear that I will never be enough. Someone else will always be doing better than me.

4/ “You studied so much and you’re doing this?”

We hear that if I make my own choices in life, that will never be accepted.

5/ “You’ve gotten a little healthy.”

We hear that we’re meeting after a year and the first thing anyone sees is my body.

They must think that they care about you, they care for you.

But the way we receive it is what our mind tells us.

When a child is punished for the truth, they don’t stop doing the thing.

They just get better at hiding it.

Fear doesn’t build honesty. 
It builds distance. 
It teaches a child that the safest option is to never let you see who they really are.

The kids who grow up telling their parents the truth aren’t the ones who were scared into it.They’re the ones who knew the truth was safe.

This will be a slightly controversial take.

Living in Mumbai on ₹1 lakh a month, or at your home, your village, your city, ₹60,000 a month.

Many people will say the financially right decision is to stay at your home. 
There’s no rent, work-life balance is much better, and expenses are lower.

I say, live in Mumbai.

Live in Mumbai for the first five years of your life.

Absorb the energy of that city.

Meet people.

Go into those rooms that scare you to enter.

Because by the time you turn 35, your network will handle everything.

But at 35, you won’t build your network again.

Would you agree?
